headline: High: Goose’s default filesystem and network capabilities create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with a read-only docs list that can be treated as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a docs-only list with no ingestion surface, but Agent B reads/writes the filesystem and uses MCP/extensions, so A’s content can be copied into B or stored in shared files and then treated as instructions. The pairwise bridge is indirect, not provably absent, so the interaction exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Agent A content is copied into a file or MCP payload that Agent B reads as instructions
IF Agent B processes shared workspace text without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep A outputs in a separate read-only note, not the shared cwd
Disable MCP extensions for the session
Require explicit provenance labels on any text passed from A to B
Use a separate workspace directory for B
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping before B ingests A-derived text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, but Agent B reads files in cwd and has broad network egress, so any sensitive files present in the shared workspace can flow out through B. The pair is not documented as isolated, and B’s default filesystem access makes leakage plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the cwd or another path readable by Agent B
IF Agent B sends file contents to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running B
Run B in a dedicated empty directory
Rotate any credentials that may already be in cwd
Restrict B’s network egress at the host or container level
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution surface, but Agent B can write the filesystem, execute shell, and modify git state with shared state via filesystem. If both are pointed at the same repo or directory, B can overwrite artifacts or git metadata that A’s curated content references, creating an unsafe write-conflict pathway. Uncertainty about A’s runtime role escalates to the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same writable directory or git repository
IF Agent B performs writes while Agent A’s outputs are used as shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate directories to A and B
Avoid concurrent git operations in the same repo
Pause B before any write-heavy task
Use a lock file or single-writer policy
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a curated list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references; Agent B can act on files and shell commands. That creates a plausible chain where A’s content is copied into B and then used without verification. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Agent B uses A-derived text as source material without independent verification
IF B is allowed to execute shell or write files based on that text
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A-derived facts
Mark A content as non-authoritative in prompts
Have B cite original sources, not the list entry
Limit B to read-only summarization when consuming A outputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class is identified for A, while B is open-source and handles source code and cwd files. The only clear compliance issue is a generic workspace-handling mismatch, not a documented residency or certification conflict. Because the pair lacks evidence of regulated data flow, severity stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is placed in the shared cwd
IF B’s logs or provider calls retain that data beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review B’s retention settings before use
Use synthetic or redacted inputs
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per agent
